question: to the Commission César Luena (S&D) Subject:

Though the Nature Restoration Regulation set 1 September 2026 as the deadline for Member States to submit their draft national restoration plans (NRPs), only eight countries have done so to date. Upon receiving an NRP, the Commission has six months to provide an assessment and feedback, after which the Member State in question has another six months to submit its final plan. In view of the above: 1.
When does the Commission expect to receive the remaining 19 draft NRPs, and what information has it received from the Member States in question?
What action is the Commission taking with regard to the Member States that have failed to meet this deadline?
How will the Commission ensure that these delays do not adversely affect the Regulation’s implementation timeline or compromise its targets for 2030?
